neighborhoods.summary: East Wickham is a district in south-east London, England, within the London Borough of Bexley. It is situated north of Welling, east of Shooter's Hill, south of Plumstead, south-west of Abbey Wood and west of West Heath, and east-southeast of Charing Cross.

neighborhoods.name: Rayners Lane
neighborhoods.summary: Rayners Lane is a suburban district in the London Borough of Harrow that forms the western part of Harrow in northwest London. Located between Pinner and West Harrow, it takes its name from a road in the area, also called Rayners Lane which runs from Marsh Road in Pinner to Eastcote Lane in South Harrow.

neighborhoods.name: South Harrow
neighborhoods.summary: South Harrow is the southern part of the town of Harrow, south-west of Harrow on the Hill in the London Borough of Harrow. Its development originally spread south and west from the hamlet of Roxeth in the urbanisation process and easier access from Central London by rail.

neighborhoods.name: Harrow Weald
neighborhoods.summary: Harrow Weald is a suburban district in Greater London, England. Located about north of Harrow, Harrow Weald is formed from a leafy 1930s suburban development along with ancient woodland of Harrow Weald Common.

neighborhoods.name: Grahame Park
neighborhoods.summary: Grahame Park, located on the site of the old Hendon Aerodrome in North West London, is a north London housing estate in the London Borough of Barnet, including 1,777 council homes built in the 1970s.

neighborhoods.name: Muswell Hill
neighborhoods.summary: Muswell Hill is a district of the London Borough of Haringey, in north London, England. The hill, which reaches over above sea level, is situated north of Charing Cross.

neighborhoods.name: Stroud Green
neighborhoods.summary: Stroud Green is a suburb in north London, England, split between the London boroughs of Haringey and Islington. On its south-western side, Stroud Green Road ' forms part of the boundary between the two boroughs.

neighborhoods.name: Colney Hatch
neighborhoods.summary: Colney Hatch is the historical name for a small district within the London Borough of Barnet in London, England. Colney Hatch refers to a loosely defined area centred on the northern end of Colney Hatch Lane, which connects Friern Barnet with Muswell Hill, crossing the North Circular Road.

neighborhoods.name: Tufnell Park
neighborhoods.summary: Tufnell Park is an area in north London, England, in the London boroughs of Islington and Camden. The neighbourhood is served by Tufnell Park tube station on the Northern Line.

neighborhoods.name: Fortis Green
neighborhoods.summary: Fortis Green is a locality in the extreme northwestern corner of the Borough of Haringey, north London. It is also the name of the road that runs between Muswell Hill and East Finchley which forms part of the A504.

neighborhoods.name: Whipps Cross
neighborhoods.summary: Whipps Cross is an area of the districts of Leytonstone and Walthamstow in the London Borough of Waltham Forest in east London, England. It is most famous for Whipps Cross University Hospital.

neighborhoods.name: West Hackney
neighborhoods.summary: West Hackney is a district in the London Borough of Hackney, situated on the eastern side of Ermine Street, the major Roman Road better known as the A10. The area was part of the Ancient Parish and subsequent Metropolitan Borough of Hackney, but has come to be seen by many as an informal extension of Stoke Newington, as well as a sub-district of Hackney proper.

neighborhoods.name: Highams Park
neighborhoods.summary: Highams Park is a suburban district in east London, England, within the London Borough of Waltham Forest, north-east of Charing Cross. It sits on the western edge of Epping Forest, with Chingford Hatch to the north, Woodford to the east, Hale End and Walthamstow to the south, and Chingford Mount to the west.

neighborhoods.name: Enfield Lock
neighborhoods.summary: Enfield Lock is an area in the London Borough of Enfield, north London. It is approximately located east of the Hertford Road between Turkey Street and the Holmesdale Tunnel overpass, and extends to the River Lee Navigation, including Enfield Island Village.

neighborhoods.name: Enfield Wash
neighborhoods.summary: Enfield Wash is an area in the London Borough of Enfield, North London. It is approximately located in the area either side of Hertford Road between Ordnance Road/Turkey Street and Bell Lane/Hoe Lane.

neighborhoods.name: Newbury Park
neighborhoods.summary: Newbury Park is an area of Ilford in east London situated in the London Borough of Redbridge east of Gants Hill. The main road is the Eastern Avenue, which until the 1920s was a country lane called Hatch Lane.

neighborhoods.name: Emerson Park
neighborhoods.summary: Emerson Park is a suburban neighbourhood in the London Borough of Havering, east London. The neighbourhood developed as two large housing estates built on the estate of Nelmes manor in the parish of Hornchurch.

neighborhoods.name: Upper Norwood
neighborhoods.summary: Upper Norwood is an area of south London, England, within the London Boroughs of Bromley, Croydon, Lambeth and Southwark. It is north of Croydon.

neighborhoods.name: Pollards Hill
neighborhoods.summary: Pollards Hill is a small residential district straddling the south London boroughs of Croydon and Merton between Mitcham, Norbury and Thornton Heath. The boundary of the two boroughs is crossed by three streets which change name as each side was planned by modern local government systems, also leading to differing architecture.

neighborhoods.name: South Norwood
neighborhoods.summary: South Norwood is a district of South London, England, within the London Borough of Croydon, Greater London and formerly in the historic county of Surrey. It is located 7.8 miles south-east of Charing Cross, north of Woodside and Addiscombe, east of Selhurst and Thornton Heath, south of Crystal Palace/Upper Norwood and Anerley, and south-west of Penge.

neighborhoods.name: Monks Orchard
neighborhoods.summary: Monks Orchard is a suburb on the edge of the London Borough of Croydon, in the ceremonial county of Greater London, England, prior to 1965 it was located in the historical county of Surrey. It is situated about 10 miles south south-east of Charing Cross, south of Elmers End and Eden Park, west of West Wickham, and north and east of Shirley and Shirley Oaks.

neighborhoods.name: Harmondsworth
neighborhoods.summary: Harmondsworth is a village in the London Borough of Hillingdon in the county of Greater London with a short border to the south onto London Heathrow Airport and close to the Berkshire county border. The village has no railway stations, but adjoins the M4 motorway and the A4 road.

neighborhoods.name: Kingston Vale
neighborhoods.summary: Kingston Vale with Kingston Hill is a district in the Royal Borough of Kingston upon Thames in south-west London. It is a residential area between Richmond Park, the much smaller Putney Vale, Wimbledon Common, Coombe/Coombe Hill and the Norbiton part of the very old borough.

neighborhoods.name: Knightsbridge
neighborhoods.summary: Knightsbridge is a residential and retail district in central London, south of Hyde Park. It is identified in the London Plan as one of two international retail centres in London, alongside the West End.

neighborhoods.name: Swiss Cottage
neighborhoods.summary: Swiss Cottage is an area in the London Borough of Camden, England. It is centred on the junction of Avenue Road and Finchley Road and includes Swiss Cottage tube station.

neighborhoods.name: Covent Garden
neighborhoods.summary: Covent Garden is a district in London, on the eastern fringes of the West End, between St Martin's Lane and Drury Lane. It is associated with the former fruit-and-vegetable market in the central square, now a popular shopping and tourist site, and with the Royal Opera House, itself known as "Covent Garden".

neighborhoods.name: Hatton Garden
neighborhoods.summary: Hatton Garden is a shopping street and commercial area in the London Borough of Camden. The area, which is London's principal diamond and jewellery quarter, is located in Holborn, on the fringe of London's West End.

neighborhoods.name: Primrose Hill
neighborhoods.summary: Primrose Hill is a district in the London Borough of Camden, England. The area east of the park was developed and became known as Primrose Hill.

neighborhoods.name: Bourne Estate
neighborhoods.summary: The Bourne Estate is an Edwardian housing estate in Holborn, located in the London Borough of Camden. It is bounded by Clerkenwell Road to the north, Gray's Inn Road to the west, Leather Lane to the east and Baldwins Gardens to the south.

neighborhoods.name: Sutton Estate
neighborhoods.summary: Sutton Dwellings, also known as the Sutton Estate, are a series of 14 residential buildings in Chelsea, London, United Kingdom.

neighborhoods.name: Catford South
neighborhoods.summary: Catford is a district in south-east London, England, and the administrative centre of the London Borough of Lewisham. It is southwest of Lewisham itself, mostly in the Rushey Green and Catford South wards.

neighborhoods.name: Samuda Estate
neighborhoods.summary: The Samuda Estate is on the east side of Manchester Road, in Cubitt Town on the Isle of Dogs. With 505 dwellings it is home to about 1,500 people and covers .

neighborhoods.name: Little Ilford
neighborhoods.summary: Little Ilford is a district of London, England in the London Borough of Newham. It gives its name to the Little Ilford ward.

neighborhoods.name: Shooters Hill
neighborhoods.summary: Shooter's Hill is a district of South East London, England, straddling the Royal Borough of Greenwich and the London Borough of Bexley. It lies north of Eltham and south of Woolwich.

neighborhoods.name: North Wembley
neighborhoods.summary: North Wembley is a locality in Wembley in the north-west of London, England. It is located in the London Borough of Brent, close to the London Borough of Harrow boundary.

neighborhoods.name: Friern Barnet
neighborhoods.summary: Friern Barnet is a suburban area within the London Borough of Barnet, north of Charing Cross. Its centre is formed by the busy intersection of Colney Hatch Lane, Woodhouse Road and Friern Barnet Road.

neighborhoods.name: Palmers Green
neighborhoods.summary: Palmers Green is a suburban area in north London, England, within the London Borough of Enfield. It is located within the N13 postcode district, around north of Charing Cross.

neighborhoods.name: New Southgate
neighborhoods.summary: New Southgate is a residential suburb straddling three Outer London Boroughs: a small part of the east of Barnet, a south-west corner of Enfield and in loosest definitions, based on nearest railway stations, a small northern corner of Haringey in North London, England, where estates merge into Bounds Green. Its first church, founded in 1873, was among organisations opting for the newer name, New Southgate, rather than the older hamlet name Colney Hatch, which from 1851 became more use-specific.

neighborhoods.name: Woodside Park
neighborhoods.summary: Woodside Park is a suburban residential area in the London Borough of Barnet, in the North Finchley postal district of N12.

neighborhoods.name: Golders Green
neighborhoods.summary: Golders Green is a suburb in the London Borough of Barnet in north West London, northwest of Charing Cross. Its historical origins lie in a medieval small suburban linear settlement that was sited near a farm and public grazing area green.

neighborhoods.name: Finsbury Park
neighborhoods.summary: Finsbury Park is an area in north London, England, which grew up around an important railway interchange near the convergence of the Boroughs of Islington and Hackney and is named after the park in Haringey. Finsbury Park should not be confused with Finsbury, which is a district of Central London roughly three miles to the south, forming the south-eastern part of the London Borough of Islington.

neighborhoods.name: Seven Sisters
neighborhoods.summary: Seven Sisters is a district of Tottenham, north London, England, at the eastern end of Seven Sisters Road, which runs from Tottenham High Road to join the A1 in Holloway.

neighborhoods.name: Stamford Hill
neighborhoods.summary: Stamford Hill is an area in North London, England, about northeast of Charing Cross. The neighbourhood is primarily located in the London Borough of Hackney, with its northern section extending into the London Borough of Haringey, and is known for its Hasidic community, the largest concentration of orthodox Ashkenazi in Europe.

neighborhoods.name: Worcester Park
neighborhoods.summary: Worcester Park is a suburban town in south-west London and Surrey, England. It lies partly in the London Borough of Sutton and partly in the Surrey borough of Epsom and Ewell, while its post town also covers part of the Old Malden district of the Royal Borough of Kingston upon Thames.

neighborhoods.name: Seething Wells
neighborhoods.summary: Seething Wells is a neighbourhood in southwest London on the border between Surbiton in the Royal Borough of Kingston upon Thames in Greater London, and Elmbridge in Surrey. The area was historically a waterworks that supplied London with water from the River Thames.

neighborhoods.name: Thornton Heath
neighborhoods.summary: Thornton Heath is a district of South London, England, within the London Borough of Croydon. It is around north of the town of Croydon, and south of Charing Cross.

neighborhoods.name: Collier's Wood
neighborhoods.summary: Colliers Wood is an area in southwest London, England, in the London Borough of Merton. It is a mostly residential area, but has a busy high street around Colliers Wood tube station on London Underground's Northern line.

neighborhoods.name: Crystal Palace
neighborhoods.summary: Crystal Palace is a place in South London, named after the Crystal Palace Exhibition building which stood in the area from 1854, until it was destroyed by a fire in 1936. About southeast of Charing Cross, it includes one of the highest points in London, at , offering views over the capital.

neighborhoods.name: Bromley Common
neighborhoods.summary: Bromley Common is an unincorporated village in Greater London, within the London Borough of Bromley. Prior to 1965 it was within the historic county of Kent.

neighborhoods.name: St Paul's Cray
neighborhoods.summary: St Paul's Cray is a suburb of Orpington within the London Borough of Bromley, Greater London. Prior to 1965 it was within the historic county of Kent.

neighborhoods.name: Old Oak Common
neighborhoods.summary: Old Oak Common is a semi-industrial area of London, between Harlesden and Acton. The area is traditionally known for its railway depots, particularly Old Oak Common TMD which was decommissioned in 2021.

neighborhoods.name: West Hampstead
neighborhoods.summary: West Hampstead is an area in the London Borough of Camden. Neighbouring areas includes Childs Hill to the north, Frognal to the east, Swiss Cottage to the south-east, South Hampstead to the south and Kilburn to the south-west.

neighborhoods.name: Parson's Green
neighborhoods.summary: Parsons Green is a mainly residential district in the London Borough of Hammersmith and Fulham. The Green itself, which is roughly triangular, is bounded on two of its three sides by the New King's Road section of the King's Road, A308 road and Parsons Green Lane.

neighborhoods.name: Wimbledon Park
neighborhoods.summary: Wimbledon Park is the name of an urban park in Wimbledon and also of the suburb south and east of the park and the Wimbledon Park tube station. The park itself is in area.

neighborhoods.name: Wimbledon Village
neighborhoods.summary: Wimbledon Park is the name of an urban park in Wimbledon and also of the suburb south and east of the park and the Wimbledon Park tube station. The park itself is in area.

neighborhoods.name: Pullens Estate
neighborhoods.summary: The Pullens Buildings, also known as the Pullens Estate, are some of the last Victorian tenement buildings surviving in London, England. In the Walworth, Newington area, they are near Elephant and Castle and Kennington Underground stations.

neighborhoods.name: Dolphin Square
neighborhoods.summary: Dolphin Square is a prominent estate of private flats near the River Thames in Pimlico, Westminster, UK. Built between 1935 and 1937, it was, until the development of Highbury Square, the largest garden square in Greater London constructed as private housing.

neighborhoods.name: Bromley-by-Bow
neighborhoods.summary: Bromley or Bromley-by-Bow is a district in the London Borough of Tower Hamlets in East London, located on the western banks of the River Lea, in the Lower Lea Valley in East London. It is an inner-city suburb located 4.7 miles east of Charing Cross.

neighborhoods.name: Butler's Wharf
neighborhoods.summary: Butler's Wharf is an English historic building at Shad Thames on the south bank of the River Thames, just east of London's Tower Bridge, now housing luxury flats and restaurants. Lying between Shad Thames and the Thames Path, it overlooks both the bridge and St Katharine Docks on the north side of the river.

neighborhoods.name: Telegraph Hill
neighborhoods.summary: Telegraph Hill is a largely residential conservation area bounded by Nunhead and Brockley and is an electoral ward just south of New Cross in the London Borough of Lewisham in southeast London, England.

neighborhoods.name: New Era Estate
neighborhoods.summary: The New Era estate is a housing estate in Hoxton, in the London Borough of Hackney, part of East London. Approximately 100 families lived on the estate in 2015.

neighborhoods.name: Burrells Wharf
neighborhoods.summary: Burrells Wharf is a riverside residential estate, owned by its leaseholders, in London, England. It is situated on the Isle of Dogs and the north bank of the River Thames.

neighborhoods.name: Morden College
neighborhoods.summary: Morden College is a charity which has been providing residential care in Blackheath, south-east London, England for over 300 years. Founded by philanthropist Sir John Morden in 1695 as a home for "poor Merchants", Morden College was built to a design sometimes attributed to Sir Christopher Wren.

neighborhoods.name: Regents Estate
neighborhoods.summary: Regent Estate is a housing estate in Hackney located in the London Borough of Hackney. The estate is named in reference to the nearby Regent's Canal, which was commissioned by the Prince Regent who later became King George IV.

neighborhoods.name: North Woolwich
neighborhoods.summary: North Woolwich is an area in the London Borough of Newham in East London, England, on the northern bank of the River Thames, across the river from Woolwich. It is connected to Woolwich by the Woolwich Ferry and Woolwich foot tunnel.

neighborhoods.name: Lessness Heath
neighborhoods.summary: Lessness Heath is a district in the London Borough of Bexley, in the area of Belvedere.

neighborhoods.name: Winchmore Hill
neighborhoods.summary: Winchmore Hill is a suburb in the London Borough of Enfield, north London, England, in the N21 postal district. The Winchmore Hill conservation area serves as the focal point of the district.

neighborhoods.name: North Finchley
neighborhoods.summary: North Finchley is a suburb of London in the London Borough of Barnet, situated north-northwest of Charing Cross. North Finchley is centred on Tally Ho Corner, the junction of the roads to East Finchley, Church End, Friern Barnet and Whetstone.

neighborhoods.name: Temple Fortune
neighborhoods.summary: Temple Fortune is a place in the London Borough of Barnet to the north of Golders Green. It is principally a shopping district used by residents of the Hampstead Garden Suburb.

neighborhoods.name: Brunswick Park
neighborhoods.summary: Brunswick Park is a neighbourhood and public park in the London Borough of Barnet. It is north of New Southgate and to the south of Oakleigh Park.

neighborhoods.name: Dartmouth Park
neighborhoods.summary: Dartmouth Park is a district of the London Borough of Camden, north of Charing Cross. The area adjoins Highgate and Highgate Cemetery, Kentish Town and Hampstead Heath is to the west.

neighborhoods.name: Andover Estate
neighborhoods.summary: The Andover Estate, in Holloway, North London, is a large Islington London Borough Council housing estate which is flanked by Hornsey Road, Seven Sisters Road, Durham Road and Birnam Road. It falls into the N7 postcode district of London.

neighborhoods.name: Tottenham Hale
neighborhoods.summary: Tottenham Hale is a district of north London and part of the London Borough of Haringey, bounded by the River Lea and located to the south/south-east of Tottenham proper. From 1850 to 1965, it was part of the Municipal Borough of Tottenham, in Middlesex.

neighborhoods.name: Bush Hill Park
neighborhoods.summary: Bush Hill Park is an area of Enfield, located to the south-east of Enfield Town, on the outskirts of north London, and historically in Middlesex. Much of the district is a planned suburban estate, developed mainly in the late-19th and early-20th centuries, and designated a conservation area in 1986.

neighborhoods.name: South Woodford
neighborhoods.summary: South Woodford is an area of east London, England, within the London Borough of Redbridge. It adjoins Woodford Green to the north, Walthamstow to the west, Snaresbrook and Wanstead to the south and Redbridge to the east, and is north-east of Charing Cross.

neighborhoods.name: Woodford Green
neighborhoods.summary: Woodford Green is an affluent area of Woodford in East London, England, within the London Borough of Redbridge. It adjoins Buckhurst Hill to the north, Woodford Bridge to the east, South Woodford to the south, and Chingford to the west.

neighborhoods.name: Chadwell Heath
neighborhoods.summary: Chadwell Heath is an area in East London, England. It is split between the London Borough of Barking and Dagenham and the London Borough of Redbridge, around west of Romford and east of Ilford, and north-east of Charing Cross.

neighborhoods.name: Ardleigh Green
neighborhoods.summary: Ardleigh Green is an area in east London, England, within the London Borough of Havering. It is east-northeast of Charing Cross.

neighborhoods.name: Gallows Corner
neighborhoods.summary: Gallows Corner is a major road junction in the London Borough of Havering, East London. It forms the junction of the A12 road with the A127 Southend Arterial Road.

neighborhoods.name: South Wimbledon
neighborhoods.summary: South Wimbledon is an area of Wimbledon in south-west London in the London Borough of Merton, England.

neighborhoods.name: Strawberry Hill
neighborhoods.summary: Strawberry Hill is an area of the London Borough of Richmond upon Thames in Twickenham. It is a suburban development situated 10.4 miles west south-west of Charing Cross.

neighborhoods.name: Shepherd's Bush
neighborhoods.summary: Shepherd's Bush is a suburb of West London, England, within the London Borough of Hammersmith and Fulham west of Charing Cross, and identified as a major metropolitan centre in the London Plan. Although primarily residential in character, its focus is the shopping area of Shepherd's Bush Green, with the Westfield London shopping centre a short distance to the north.

neighborhoods.name: West Kensington
neighborhoods.summary: West Kensington, formerly North End, is an area in the ancient parish of Fulham, in the London Borough of Hammersmith and Fulham, England, 3.4 miles west of Charing Cross. It covers most of the London postal area of W14, including the area around Barons Court tube station, and is defined as the area between Lillie Road to the south, Fulham Palace Road to the west, Hammersmith Road to the north, and West Brompton and Earl's Court to the east.

neighborhoods.name: St. John's Wood
neighborhoods.summary: St John's Wood is a district in the City of Westminster, London, England, about 2.5 miles northwest of Charing Cross. Historically the northern part of the ancient parish and Metropolitan Borough of Marylebone, it extends from Regent's Park and Primrose Hill in the east to Edgware Road in the west, with the Swiss Cottage area of Hampstead to the north and Lisson Grove to the south.

neighborhoods.name: West Smithfield
neighborhoods.summary: Smithfield, properly known as West Smithfield, is a district located in Central London, part of Farringdon Without, the most westerly ward of the City of London, England. Smithfield is home to a number of City institutions, such as St Bartholomew's Hospital and livery halls, including those of the Butchers' and Haberdashers' Companies.

neighborhoods.name: Finsbury Estate
neighborhoods.summary: Finsbury Estate is a large-scale housing estate in the Clerkenwell area of London, England, comprising four purpose-built blocks of flats located on a level site, providing 451 residences. Patrick Coman House and Michael Cliffe House are high-rise blocks of 9 and 25 storeys respectively, while Joseph Trotter House and Charles Townsend House are of four storeys.

neighborhoods.name: Bemerton Estate
neighborhoods.summary: The Bemerton Estate is a social housing estate to the north of Bingfield Street and west of Caledonian Road, in the London Borough of Islington. It was built between 1969 to 1973, and named after Bemerton Street, the northern part of which it replaced.

neighborhoods.name: Dulwich Village
neighborhoods.summary: Dulwich Village is an affluent area of Dulwich in South London, England. It is located in the London Borough of Southwark.

neighborhoods.name: Lower Belvedere
neighborhoods.summary: Belvedere is a town in south east London, England, within the London Borough of Bexley. It lies close to the River Thames, with Erith to the east, Bexleyheath to the south, and Abbey Wood and Thamesmead to the west.

neighborhoods.name: Orchard Village
neighborhoods.summary: Orchard Village, on the site of the former Mardyke Estate, is a housing development in the South Hornchurch area of London, England. From 2009 to 2017 the site underwent regeneration as part of the London Riverside part of the Thames Gateway.

neighborhoods.name: Brownswood Park
neighborhoods.summary: Brownswood is a ward in the London Borough of Hackney and forms part of the Hackney North and Stoke Newington constituency. The ward has existed since the creation of the borough on 1 April 1965 and was first used in the 1964 elections.

neighborhoods.name: Duckett's Green
neighborhoods.summary: Duckett's Green is an area of north London, England in the United Kingdom and part of the London Borough of Haringey. It is an inner-suburban area located 5.8 miles north of Charing Cross.

neighborhoods.name: Stoke Newington
neighborhoods.summary: Stoke Newington is an area in North London, England, located in the northwest part of the London Borough of Hackney. The area is northeast of Charing Cross.

neighborhoods.name: Broadwater Farm
neighborhoods.summary: Broadwater Farm, often referred to simply as "The Farm", is an area in Tottenham, North London, straddling the River Moselle. The eastern half of the area is dominated by the Broadwater Farm Estate, an experiment in high-density social housing, loosely based on Corbusian ideas, dominated by concrete towers connected by walkways, built in the late 1960s using cheap but fire-vulnerable pre-fabricated concrete panels.

neighborhoods.name: Enfield Highway
neighborhoods.summary: Enfield Highway is an area in the London Borough of Enfield, north London. It is roughly located in the area either side of Hertford Road between Hoe Lane and The Ride.

neighborhoods.name: Chingford Mount
neighborhoods.summary: Chingford Mount is an area of Chingford, east London, England, located in South Chingford. The name refers to the shopping area located around A112/A1009 crossroads, though it is also used for the hill leading north from the crossroads to Chingford Old Church.

neighborhoods.name: South Chingford
neighborhoods.summary: South Chingford is a largely residential area of Chingford in east London, England.

neighborhoods.name: Becontree Heath
neighborhoods.summary: Becontree Heath is an open space in the London Borough of Barking and Dagenham. The name has also been applied to the local area, in particular to the RM8 postal district.

neighborhoods.name: Woodford Bridge
neighborhoods.summary: Woodford Bridge is part of the East London suburb of Woodford, in the London Borough of Redbridge. It is on an old road between Chigwell and Leytonstone.

neighborhoods.name: Tooting Graveney
neighborhoods.summary: Tooting is a district in South London, forming part of the London Borough of Wandsworth. It is located south south-west of Charing Cross.

neighborhoods.name: South Kensington
neighborhoods.summary: South Kensington is a district at the West End of Central London in the Royal Borough of Kensington and Chelsea. Historically it settled on part of the scattered Middlesex village of Brompton.

neighborhoods.name: North Kensington
neighborhoods.summary: North Kensington is an area of west London. It is north of Notting Hill and south of Kensal Green predominantly in the Royal Borough of Kensington and Chelsea and partly in the London Borough of Brent and City of Westminster.

neighborhoods.name: Brondesbury Park
neighborhoods.summary: Brondesbury Park is a suburb in the London Borough of Brent, centred on Brondesbury Park railway station and the street, an avenue, which shares its name. The area has a number of open spaces, primarily Queen's Park and Tiverton Green.

neighborhoods.name: Hallfield Estate
neighborhoods.summary: The Hallfield Estate is one of several modernist housing projects in Bayswater, City of Westminster, and was designed in the immediate postwar period by the Tecton architecture practice, led by Berthold Lubetkin. Following the dissolution of Tecton, the project was realised by Denys Lasdun and Lindsay Drake in the 1950s.

neighborhoods.name: De Beauvoir Town
neighborhoods.summary: De Beauvoir Town is a neighbourhood in the London Borough of Hackney, north of the City of London. It is sometimes described as a part of Dalston.

neighborhoods.name: Aylesbury Estate
neighborhoods.summary: The Aylesbury Estate is a large housing estate located in Walworth, South East London. The Aylesbury Estate contains 2,704 dwellings, spread over a number of different blocks and buildings, and was built between 1963 and 1977.

neighborhoods.name: Excalibur Estate
neighborhoods.summary: The Excalibur Estate was a post-war 1940s housing estate of 189 prefabricated houses in Catford, South London. The estate contained the last sizeable collection of post-war prefabricated houses in the United Kingdom.

neighborhoods.name: South Hornchurch
neighborhoods.summary: South Hornchurch is a locality to the south of Hornchurch in London Borough of Havering, east London. It is a suburban development situated 13.6 miles east of Charing Cross.

neighborhoods.name: Upminster Bridge
neighborhoods.summary: Upminster Bridge is a crossing of the River Ingrebourne carrying the A124 road between the suburbs of Hornchurch and Upminster in northeast London, England. The bridge is known to have existed since at least 1375 and the current brick bridge was opened in 1892, replacing a series of wooden bridges.

neighborhoods.name: Foots Cray Estate
neighborhoods.summary: Foots Cray is an area of South East London, England, within the London Borough of Bexley. Prior to 1965 it was in the historic county of Kent.

neighborhoods.name: White City Estate
neighborhoods.summary: White City is a district of London, England, in the northern part of Shepherd's Bush in the London Borough of Hammersmith and Fulham, 5 miles west-northwest of Charing Cross. White City is home to Television Centre, White City Place, Westfield London and Loftus Road, the home stadium of Queens Park Rangers F.C.

neighborhoods.name: Caledonian Estate
neighborhoods.summary: The Caledonian Estate is a Grade II listed, early Edwardian estate towards the northern end of the Caledonian Road in Islington, London. It is situated next to Pentonville Prison.

neighborhoods.name: Kidbrooke Village
neighborhoods.summary: Kidbrooke Village is a residential development located in the Kidbrooke area of the Royal Borough of Greenwich, in London, England. It is part of a larger regeneration project aimed at transforming the former Ferrier Estate into a new, mixed-use community.

neighborhoods.name: Carpenters Estate
neighborhoods.summary: The Carpenters Estate is located in Stratford, Newham, East London, close to the Queen Elizabeth Olympic Park. The estate is formed of low rise social housing and three tower blocks.

neighborhoods.name: Aberfeldy Village
neighborhoods.summary: Aberfeldy Village is an urban village in Poplar, London, England, which is in the process of being redeveloped in a joint venture between Poplar HARCA and Willmott Dixon. It was known as the Aberfeldy Estate, a housing estate but has expanded.

neighborhoods.name: Barking Riverside
neighborhoods.summary: Barking Riverside is a mixed-use development in the area of Barking, east London, England, within the London Borough of Barking and Dagenham. It is being built on land formerly occupied by Barking Power Station, adjacent to the River Thames, and is 10.5 miles east of Charing Cross.

neighborhoods.name: Woolwich Dockyard
neighborhoods.summary: Woolwich Dockyard was an English naval dockyard along the river Thames at Woolwich—originally in north-west Kent, now in southeast London—where many ships were built from the early 16th century until the late 19th century. William Camden called it 'the Mother Dock of all England'.

neighborhoods.name: Upper Walthamstow
neighborhoods.summary: Walthamstow is a town within the London Borough of Waltham Forest in East London. The town borders Chingford to the north, Snaresbrook and South Woodford to the east, Leyton and Leytonstone to the south, and Tottenham to the west.

neighborhoods.name: Green Street Green
neighborhoods.summary: Green Street Green is an area in south-east London, located in the London Borough of Bromley and, prior to 1965, in the historic county of Kent. It is located south of Orpington, west of Chelsfield, north-west of Pratt's Bottom, north of Hazelwood, and south east of Farnborough.

neighborhoods.name: Saint George Wharf
neighborhoods.summary: St George Wharf is a riverside development in Vauxhall, Lambeth, London, England, located on the southern bank of the River Thames beside Vauxhall Bridge. Vauxhall Pier is a calling point for Uber Boat by Thames Clippers riverboats RB1 and RB6 services.

neighborhoods.name: Golden Lane Estate
neighborhoods.summary: The Golden Lane Estate is a 1950s council housing complex in the City of London. It was built on the northern edge of the City, on a site devastated by bombing during the Second World War.

neighborhoods.name: Chelsea Waterfront
neighborhoods.summary: Chelsea Waterfront is a residential development in Chelsea in West London. It consists largely of the disused Lots Road Power Station which was refurbished for residential use, and two highrises of and .

neighborhoods.name: Charlton Riverside
neighborhoods.summary: Charlton Riverside, previously known as New Charlton, is the area along the south bank of the river Thames at Charlton, London, which forms part of the Royal Borough of Greenwich. It was formerly a primarily industrial zone, known for the glass and rope making industries, but is now an area of regeneration.

neighborhoods.name: Harrow on the Hill
neighborhoods.summary: Harrow on the Hill or Harrow-on-the-Hill is an area and historic village in the London Borough of Harrow in north-west London, England. The name refers to Harrow Hill, , and is located some half a mile south of the modern town of Harrow.

neighborhoods.name: Whittington Estate
neighborhoods.summary: The Whittington Estate, also known as Highgate New Town, is a housing estate in the London Borough of Camden, North London, England. It was designed in a modernist style by Peter Tábori and Ken Adie for Camden Council's Architects Department.

neighborhoods.name: Elephant and Castle
neighborhoods.summary: Elephant and Castle is an area of south London, England, in the London Borough of Southwark. The name also informally refers to much of Walworth and Newington, due to the proximity of the London Underground station of the same name.

neighborhoods.name: Lisson Green Estate
neighborhoods.summary: Lisson Grove is a street and district in the City of Westminster in London, England. The neighbourhood contains a few important cultural landmarks, including Lisson Gallery, Alfies Antique Market, Red Bus Recording Studios, the former Christ Church, now the Greenhouse Centre, Stringers of London and the Seashell of Lisson Grove.

neighborhoods.name: Greenwich Peninsula
neighborhoods.summary: The Greenwich Peninsula, also known as North Greenwich, is an area of Greenwich in South East London, England. It is bounded on three sides by a loop of the Thames, between the Isle of Dogs to the west and Silvertown to the east.

neighborhoods.name: Walthamstow Village
neighborhoods.summary: Walthamstow Village is the oldest part of Walthamstow, east London. It was designated a Conservation Area by the London Borough of Waltham Forest in 1967, and another Conservation Area on nearby Orford Road was subsequently added.

neighborhoods.name: New Providence Wharf
neighborhoods.summary: The New Providence Wharf is a residential development in the Blackwall district of the London Borough of Tower Hamlets, at the north end of the Blackwall Tunnel. It was designed by Skidmore, Owings and Merrill and is managed by Ballymore, a property development company.

neighborhoods.name: Northumberland Heath
neighborhoods.summary: Northumberland Heath is an area of South East London, England within the London Borough of Bexley. It is located south of Erith and north of Bexleyheath.

neighborhoods.name: Tower Gardens Estate
neighborhoods.summary: Tower Gardens in North Tottenham is a distinctive semi-circular estate bounded by Lordship Lane and the Roundway. Constructed between 1904 and 1928 in the arts and crafts style.

neighborhoods.name: Loughborough Junction
neighborhoods.summary: Loughborough Junction is an area in Herne Hill, South London, in the London Borough of Lambeth. It is located equidistant between Herne Hill, Brixton and Camberwell providing excellent transport connections to Central London.

neighborhoods.name: Alexandra Road Estate
neighborhoods.summary: The Alexandra Road Estate is a housing estate in the London Borough of Camden, North London, England. It was designed in a brutalist style in 1968 by Neave Brown of Camden Council's Architects Department.

neighborhoods.name: Ampthill Square Estate
neighborhoods.summary: The Ampthill Square Estate, also known as the Ampthill Estate, is a housing estate in the London Borough of Camden in London, England. The estate is located in the Somers Town district, on the south side of Harrington Square, east side of Hampstead Road, and west side of Eversholt Street.

neighborhoods.name: St. George in the East
neighborhoods.summary: St George in the East, historically known as Wapping-Stepney is an area in the London Borough of Tower Hamlets, England. It was an ancient parish, it was the larger of the two parishes that made up Wapping.

neighborhoods.name: Enfield Island Village
neighborhoods.summary: Enfield Island Village is a modern housing development in the Enfield Lock area of Enfield, north London. It was built between 1997 and 2003 on land previously occupied by the Royal Small Arms Factory.

neighborhoods.name: Hampstead Garden Suburb
neighborhoods.summary: Hampstead Garden Suburb is a suburb of London, north of Hampstead, west of Highgate and east of Golders Green. It is known for its intellectual, liberal, artistic, musical and literary associations.

neighborhoods.name: Churchill Gardens Estate
neighborhoods.summary: Churchill Gardens is a large housing estate in the Pimlico area of Westminster, London. The estate was developed between 1946 and 1962 to a design by the architects Powell and Moya, replacing Victorian terraced houses extensively damaged during the Blitz.

neighborhoods.name: Lillington Gardens Estate
neighborhoods.summary: Lillington Gardens is an estate in the Pimlico area of the City of Westminster, constructed in phases between 1961 and 1971 to a plan by Darbourne & Darke. The estate was formerly owned and managed by CityWest Homes.

neighborhoods.name: Greenwich Millennium Village
neighborhoods.summary: Greenwich Millennium Village is a mixed-tenure modern development on an urban village model located on the Greenwich Peninsula in Greenwich, in south-east London, and part of the Millennium Communities Programme under English Partnerships. The village is designed by architects Ralph Erskine and partners with EPR Architects Ltd as executive architect as part of the regeneration of the whole brownfield site of East Greenwich Gas Works.

neighborhoods.name: Harringay Warehouse District
neighborhoods.summary: The Harringay Warehouse District is a part of the North London neighbourhood of Harringay in the London Borough of Haringey.

neighborhoods.name: Passy
neighborhoods.summary: Passy is an area of Paris, France, located in the 16th arrondissement, on the Right Bank. It is adjacent to Auteuil to the southwest, and Chaillot to the northeast.

neighborhoods.name: Javel
neighborhoods.summary: Javel is the 60th administrative district of Paris situated in the 15th arrondissement.

neighborhoods.name: Bercy
neighborhoods.summary: Bercy is a neighbourhood in the 12th arrondissement of Paris, France, the city's 47th administrative neighbourhood.

neighborhoods.name: Pigalle
neighborhoods.summary: Pigalle is an area in Paris, France, around the Place Pigalle, on the border between the 9th and the 18th arrondissements. It is named after the sculptor Jean-Baptiste Pigalle.

neighborhoods.name: Auteuil
neighborhoods.summary: Auteuil is the 61st and westernmost quarter of Paris, France, located in the 16th arrondissement, on the Right Bank. It is adjacent to Passy to the northeast, Boulogne-Billancourt to the southwest, and the Bois de Boulogne to the northwest.

neighborhoods.name: Sentier
neighborhoods.summary: Sentier is a neighbourhood in the 2nd arrondissement of Paris which has been known historically as a multicultural textile and garment manufacturing district. Since the late 1990s, it has increasingly become home to many Internet start-up companies and has acquired the nickname Silicon Sentier.

neighborhoods.name: Grenelle
neighborhoods.summary: Grenelle is a neighbourhood in southwestern Paris, France. It is a part of the 15th arrondissement of the city.

neighborhoods.name: Bastille
neighborhoods.summary: The Bastille was a medieval fortress in Paris, known as the Bastille Saint-Antoine. It played an important role in the internal conflicts of France and for most of its history was used as a state prison by the kings of France.

neighborhoods.name: Charonne
neighborhoods.summary: The Charonne quarter is an area of the 20th arrondissement of Paris named after a former municipality in the area, which was merged into the city of Paris in 1860 by Napoleon III and split between Charonne quarter, the Père-Lachaise quarter and Saint-Fargeau quarter. The historic centre of Charonne is located around the junction of Rue de Bagnolet and Rue Saint-Blaise, in the vicinity of the parish church of Saint-Germain-de-Charonne.

neighborhoods.name: Vaugirard
neighborhoods.summary: The 15th arrondissement of Paris is one of the 20 arrondissements of the capital city of France. In spoken French, it is referred to as.

neighborhoods.name: 15e Arrondissement
neighborhoods.summary: The 15th arrondissement of Paris is one of the 20 arrondissements of the capital city of France. In spoken French, it is referred to as.

neighborhoods.name: Invalides
neighborhoods.summary: The Hôtel des Invalides, commonly called, is a complex of buildings in the 7th arrondissement of Paris, France, containing museums and monuments, all relating to the military history of France, as well as a hospital and an old soldiers' retirement home, the building's original purpose. The buildings house the Musée de l'Armée, the Musée des Plans-Reliefs, and the Musée d'Histoire Contemporaine.

neighborhoods.name: Le Marais
neighborhoods.summary: The Marais is a historic district in Paris, France. It spreads across parts of the 3rd and 4th arrondissements on the Rive Droite, or Right Bank, of the Seine.

neighborhoods.name: Beaubourg
neighborhoods.summary: The Centre Pompidou, more fully the Centre national d'art et de culture Georges-Pompidou, also known as the Pompidou Centre in English and colloquially as Beaubourg, is a building complex in Paris, France. It was designed in the style of high-tech architecture by the architectural team of Richard Rogers, Su Rogers and Renzo Piano, along with Gianfranco Franchini.

neighborhoods.name: Montmartre
neighborhoods.summary: Montmartre is a large hill in Paris's northern 18th arrondissement. It is high and gives its name to the surrounding district, part of the Right Bank.

neighborhoods.name: Montsouris
neighborhoods.summary: Parc Montsouris is a public park situated in southern Paris, France. Located in the 14th arrondissement, it was officially inaugurated in 1875 after an early opening in 1869.

neighborhoods.name: Belleville
neighborhoods.summary: Belleville is a neighbourhood of Paris, France, parts of which lie in four different arrondissements. The major portion of Belleville straddles the borderline between the 20th arrondissement and the 19th along its main street, the Rue de Belleville.

neighborhoods.name: Batignolles
neighborhoods.summary: Batignolles is a neighbourhood of Paris, part of its 17th arrondissement. The neighbourhood is bounded on the south by the Boulevard des Batignolles, on the east by the Avenue de Clichy, on the north by Rue Cardinet and on the west by the Rue de Rome.

neighborhoods.name: La Chapelle
neighborhoods.summary: The Quartier de La Chapelle is a neighborhood of Paris, in the eastern part of the 18th arrondissement. It was originally the village of La Chapelle on the outskirts of Paris and a commune in its own right, separated from the commune of Paris by the wall of the Farmers-General.

neighborhoods.name: Montparnasse
neighborhoods.summary: Montparnasse is an area in the south of Paris, France, on the left bank of the river Seine, centred at the crossroads of the Boulevard du Montparnasse and the Rue de Rennes, between the Rue de Rennes and boulevard Raspail. It is split between the 6th, 14th, and 15th arrondissements of the city.

neighborhoods.name: Gros-Caillou
neighborhoods.summary: The Quartier du Gros-Caillou is the 28th administrative district of Paris, located in the 7th arrondissement.

neighborhoods.name: Ménilmontant
neighborhoods.summary: Ménilmontant is a neighbourhood of Paris, situated in the city's 20th arrondissement. It is roughly defined as the area north of the Père Lachaise Cemetery, south of Parc de Belleville, and between Avenue Jean-Aicard on the west and Rue Pelleport on the east.

neighborhoods.name: Quartier latin
neighborhoods.summary: The Latin Quarter of Paris is a district in Paris on the left bank of the Seine, around the Sorbonne. Located in the city's 5th and the 6th arrondissements, it is known for its concentration of universities.

neighborhoods.name: Champs-Elysées
neighborhoods.summary: The Avenue des Champs-Élysées, usually shortened to the Champs-Élysées, is an avenue in the 8th arrondissement of Paris, France. The avenue is long and wide, running between the Place de la Concorde in the east and the Place Charles de Gaulle in the west, where the Arc de Triomphe is located.

neighborhoods.name: La Goutte d'Or
neighborhoods.summary: The Goutte d'Or is a neighbourhood in Paris, located in the 18th arrondissement of Paris. The neighbourhood has large numbers of North African and sub-Saharan residents.

neighborhoods.name: Petit-Montrouge
neighborhoods.summary: The quartier du Petit-Montrouge is number 55 of the 80 quartiers administratifs in Paris. It lies in the 14th Arrondissement, in the south of the capital.

neighborhoods.name: 6e Arrondissement
neighborhoods.summary: The 6th arrondissement of Paris is one of the 20 arrondissements of the capital city of France. In spoken French, it is referred to as le sixième.

neighborhoods.name: 5e Arrondissement
neighborhoods.summary: The 5th arrondissement of Paris is one of the 20 arrondissements of Paris, the capital city of France. In spoken French, this arrondissement is referred to as le cinquième.

neighborhoods.name: 8e Arrondissement
neighborhoods.summary: The 8th arrondissement of Paris is one of the 20 arrondissements of the capital city of France. In spoken French, the arrondissement is colloquially referred to as le huitième.

neighborhoods.name: 7e Arrondissement
neighborhoods.summary: The 7th arrondissement of Paris is one of the 20 arrondissements of the capital city of France. It is known for being, along with the 16th arrondissement and the suburban commune of Neuilly-sur-Seine, among the wealthiest places in France.

neighborhoods.name: 2e Arrondissement
neighborhoods.summary: The 2nd arrondissement of Paris is one of the 20 arrondissements of the capital city of France. In spoken French, this arrondissement is colloquially referred to as deuxième.

neighborhoods.name: 9e Arrondissement
neighborhoods.summary: The 9th arrondissement of Paris is one of the twenty arrondissements of the capital city of France. In spoken French, it is referred to as.

neighborhoods.name: Butte-aux-Cailles
neighborhoods.summary: The Butte-aux-Cailles river, which once made this area important for the tannery and tissue trades, was covered over in 1860. Its route can be traced by following a series of bronze plaques embedded in the area's pavements.

neighborhoods.name: 3e Arrondissement
neighborhoods.summary: The 3rd arrondissement of Paris is one of the 20 of the capital city of France. In spoken French, this arrondissement is colloquially referred to as "" meaning "the third".

neighborhoods.name: 4e Arrondissement
neighborhoods.summary: The 4th arrondissement of Paris is one of the twenty arrondissements of Paris, the capital city of France. In spoken French, this arrondissement is referred to as .

neighborhoods.name: Paris Rive Gauche
neighborhoods.summary: Paris Rive Gauche is a new neighbourhood in the 13th arrondissement of Paris, on the left bank of the Seine. The district is bordered by the Seine, the railway tracks of Gare d'Austerlitz and the Boulevard Périphérique.

neighborhoods.name: 14e Arrondissement
neighborhoods.summary: The 14th arrondissement of Paris, officially named arrondissement de l'Observatoire, is one of the 20 arrondissements of Paris, the capital city of France. In 2023, it had a population of 136,455.

neighborhoods.name: 17e Arrondissement
neighborhoods.summary: The 17th arrondissement of Paris is one of the 20 arrondissements of the capital city of France. In spoken French, it is referred to as le dix-septième.

neighborhoods.name: 1er Arrondissement
neighborhoods.summary: The 1st arrondissement of Paris is one of the 20 arrondissements of Paris, the capital city of France. In spoken French, this arrondissement is colloquially referred to as le premier.

neighborhoods.name: 18e Arrondissement
neighborhoods.summary: The 18th arrondissement of Paris is one of the 20 arrondissements, or administrative districts, of the capital city of France. In spoken French, this arrondissement is referred to as dix-huitième.

neighborhoods.name: 16e Arrondissement
neighborhoods.summary: The 16th arrondissement of Paris is the westernmost of the 20 arrondissements of Paris, the capital city of France. Located on the city's Right Bank, it is adjacent to the 17th and 8th arrondissements to the northeast, as well as to the suburb of Boulogne-Billancourt, Hauts-de-Seine to the southwest.

neighborhoods.name: 13e Arrondissement
neighborhoods.summary: The 13th arrondissement of Paris is one of the 20 arrondissements of Paris. In spoken French, the arrondissement is referred to as le treizième.

neighborhoods.name: 10e Arrondissement
neighborhoods.summary: The 10th arrondissement of Paris is one of the 20 arrondissements of the capital city of France. In spoken French, the arrondissement is referred to as le dixième.

neighborhoods.name: 11e Arrondissement
neighborhoods.summary: The 11th arrondissement of Paris is one of the 20 arrondissements of the capital city of France. In spoken French, the arrondissement is referred to as le onzième.

neighborhoods.name: 12e Arrondissement
neighborhoods.summary: The 12th arrondissement of Paris is one of the 20 arrondissements of the capital city of France. Situated on the right bank of the River Seine, it is the easternmost arrondissement of Paris, as well as the largest by area.

neighborhoods.name: 19e Arrondissement
neighborhoods.summary: The 19th arrondissement of Paris is one of the 20 arrondissements of the capital city of France. In spoken French, this arrondissement is referred to as dix-neuvième.

neighborhoods.name: 20e Arrondissement
neighborhoods.summary: The 20th arrondissement of Paris is the last of the consecutively numbered arrondissements of the capital city of France. Also known as Ménilmontant after the Ménilmontant neighbourhood it encompasses in its northwest, it is on the right bank of the River Seine and contains some of the city's most cosmopolitan districts.

neighborhoods.name: Quartier de l'Odéon
neighborhoods.summary: The Quartier de l'Odéon is the 22nd administrative district of Paris, located in the 6th arrondissement—primarily to the north of the Jardin du Luxembourg, which it encompasses.

neighborhoods.name: Faubourg Saint-Denis
neighborhoods.summary: The Rue du Faubourg-Saint-Denis is a street in the 10th arrondissement of Paris. It crosses the arrondissement from north to south, linking the Porte Saint-Denis to La Chapelle Métro station and passing the Gare du Nord.

neighborhoods.name: Faubourg Saint-Honoré
neighborhoods.summary: The Rue du Faubourg Saint-Honoré is a street located in the 8th arrondissement of Paris, France. Relatively narrow and undistinguished, especially in comparison to the nearby Avenue des Champs-Élysées, it is cited as being one of the most luxurious and fashionable streets in the world due to the presence of major global fashion houses, including the Élysée Palace, the Hôtel de Pontalba, the Embassy of Canada, the Embassy of the United Kingdom, as well as numerous art galleries.

neighborhoods.name: Saint-Germain-des-Prés
neighborhoods.summary: Saint-Germain-des-Prés is one of the four administrative quarters of the 6th arrondissement of Paris, France, located around the church of the former Abbey of Saint-Germain-des-Prés. Its official borders are the River Seine on the north, the on the west, between the and on the east, and the on the south.

neighborhoods.name: Faubourg Saint-Germain
neighborhoods.summary: The Faubourg Saint-Germain is a historic district of Paris's Rive Gauche, France. The Faubourg has long been known as the favourite home of the French high nobility and hosts many aristocratic hôtels particuliers.

neighborhoods.name: Faubourg Saint-Antoine
neighborhoods.summary: The Faubourg Saint-Antoine was one of the traditional suburbs of Paris, France. It grew up to the east of the Bastille around the abbey of Saint-Antoine-des-Champs, and ran along the Rue du Faubourg Saint-Antoine.

neighborhoods.name: Buch
neighborhoods.summary: Buch is a German locality within the Berlin borough of Pankow. Situated on the Panke river, it is the city's northernmost quarter, chiefly known for its historic village centre and extended hospital premises.

neighborhoods.name: Gatow
neighborhoods.summary: Gatow, a district of south-western Berlin is located west of the Havelsee lake and has forested areas within its boundaries. It is within the borough of Spandau.

neighborhoods.name: Britz
neighborhoods.summary: Britz is a German locality within the Berlin borough of Neukölln.

neighborhoods.name: WISTA
neighborhoods.summary: The WISTA Science and Technology Park in Berlin-Adlershof was founded in 1991 after the dissolution of the Academy of Sciences of the German Democratic Republic at the same place. Today it covers an area of making it the largest science park in Germany.

neighborhoods.name: Tegel
neighborhoods.summary: Tegel is a locality in the Berlin borough of Reinickendorf on the shore of Lake Tegel. The Tegel locality, the second largest in area of the 96 Berlin districts, also includes the neighbourhood of Saatwinkel.

neighborhoods.name: Mitte
neighborhoods.summary: Mitte is a central section of Berlin, Germany, in the eponymous borough of Mitte. Until 2001, it was itself an autonomous district.

neighborhoods.name: Karow
neighborhoods.summary: Karow is a German locality within the Berlin borough of Pankow. Until 2001 it was part of the former Weißensee borough.

neighborhoods.name: Kladow
neighborhoods.summary: Kladow is the southernmost district of the Borough of Spandau in Berlin, Germany.

neighborhoods.name: Düppel
neighborhoods.summary: Düppel is the name of a neighbourhood as well as of an adjacent forest in the borough of Steglitz-Zehlendorf in southwestern Berlin, Germany. The neighbourhood itself is a part of the Zehlendorf locality.

neighborhoods.name: Dahlem
neighborhoods.summary: Dahlem is a locality of the Steglitz-Zehlendorf borough in southwestern Berlin. Until Berlin's 2001 administrative reform it was a part of the former borough of Zehlendorf.

neighborhoods.name: Buckow
neighborhoods.summary: Buckow is a locality within the Berlin borough of Neukölln.

neighborhoods.name: Grünau
neighborhoods.summary: Grünau is a German locality within the Berlin borough of Treptow-Köpenick. Until 2001 it was part of the former borough of Köpenick.

neighborhoods.name: Lübars
neighborhoods.summary: Lübars is a German locality within the borough of Reinickendorf, Berlin.

neighborhoods.name: Pankow
neighborhoods.summary: Pankow is the second largest and most populous borough of the German capital Berlin. In Berlin's 2001 administrative reform, it was merged with the former boroughs of Prenzlauer Berg and Weißensee; the resulting borough retained the name Pankow.

neighborhoods.name: Moabit
neighborhoods.summary: Moabit is an inner city locality in the borough of Mitte, Berlin, Germany. As of 2022, about 84,000 people lived in Moabit.

neighborhoods.name: Wannsee
neighborhoods.summary: Wannsee is a locality in the southwestern Berlin borough of Steglitz-Zehlendorf, Germany. It is the westernmost locality of Berlin.

neighborhoods.name: Westend
neighborhoods.summary: Westend is a locality of the Berlin borough Charlottenburg-Wilmersdorf in Germany. It emerged in the course of Berlin's 2001 administrative reform on the grounds of the former Charlottenburg borough.

neighborhoods.name: Staaken
neighborhoods.summary: Staaken is a locality at the western rim of Berlin within the borough of Spandau.

neighborhoods.name: Spandau
neighborhoods.summary: Spandau is the westernmost of the 12 boroughs of Berlin, situated at the confluence of the Havel and Spree rivers and extending along the western bank of the Havel. It is the smallest borough by population, but the fourth largest by land area.

neighborhoods.name: Frohnau
neighborhoods.summary: Frohnau is a locality in the Reinickendorf borough of Berlin, Germany. It lies in the extreme northern part of the city.

neighborhoods.name: Wedding
neighborhoods.summary: Wedding is a locality in the borough of Mitte, Berlin, Germany. It was a separate borough in the north-western inner city until it was fused with Tiergarten and Mitte in Berlin's 2001 administrative reform.

neighborhoods.name: Marzahn
neighborhoods.summary: Marzahn is a locality within the borough of Marzahn-Hellersdorf in Berlin. Berlin's 2001 administrative reform led to the former boroughs of Marzahn and Hellersdorf fusing into a single new borough.

neighborhoods.name: Halensee
neighborhoods.summary: Halensee is a locality of Berlin in the district of Charlottenburg-Wilmersdorf. Halensee was established as a villa and tenement settlement in about 1880, in the suburb of Wilmersdorf, which became part of Greater Berlin in 1920.

neighborhoods.name: Steglitz
neighborhoods.summary: Steglitz is a locality of the Steglitz-Zehlendorf borough in Southwestern Berlin, the capital of Germany. is derived from the Slavic name for the European goldfinch, similar to the German .

neighborhoods.name: Lankwitz
neighborhoods.summary: Lankwitz is a German locality within the borough of Steglitz-Zehlendorf, Berlin. Until 2001 it was part of the former borough of Steglitz.

neighborhoods.name: Neukölln
neighborhoods.summary: Neukölln, is one of the twelve boroughs of Berlin. It is located south-east of Berlin's center and stretches from the inner city southward to the border with Brandenburg, encompassing the eponymous quarter of Neukölln in the north, and the southern quarters of Britz, Gropiusstadt, Buckow and Rudow.

neighborhoods.name: Köpenick
neighborhoods.summary: Köpenick is a historic locality in Berlin, situated at the confluence of the rivers Dahme and Spree in the southeast of the German capital. It was formerly known as Copanic and then Cöpenick, only officially adopting the current spelling in 1931.

neighborhoods.name: Altstadt
neighborhoods.summary: Altstadt Spandau is the historic centre of the Spandau borough in the western suburbs of Berlin, situated on the right bank of the Havel river by its confluence with the Spree tributary. It arose near the site of a former Slavic gord during the German eastward expansion in the early 13th century.

neighborhoods.name: Wittenau
neighborhoods.summary: Wittenau is a German locality within the borough of Reinickendorf, Berlin.

neighborhoods.name: Biesdorf
neighborhoods.summary: Biesdorf is a locality within the Berlin borough of Marzahn-Hellersdorf. Until 2001 it was part of the former borough of Marzahn.

neighborhoods.name: Grunewald
neighborhoods.summary: Grunewald is a German forest located in the western side of Berlin on the east side of the Havel, mainly in the Grunewald locality. At it is the largest green area in the city of Berlin.

neighborhoods.name: Friedenau
neighborhoods.summary: Friedenau is a locality within the borough of Tempelhof-Schöneberg in Berlin, Germany. Relatively small by area, its population density was the highest in the city.

neighborhoods.name: Kreuzberg
neighborhoods.summary: Kreuzberg is a district of Berlin, Germany. It is part of the Friedrichshain-Kreuzberg borough located south of Mitte.

neighborhoods.name: City West
neighborhoods.summary: City West or Zooviertel) is an area in the western part of central Berlin. It is one of Berlin's main commercial areas, and was the commercial centre of former West Berlin when the city was divided by the Berlin Wall.

neighborhoods.name: Adlershof
neighborhoods.summary: Adlershof is a locality in the borough Treptow-Köpenick of Berlin, Germany. Adlershof is home to the new City of Science, Technology and Media, located on the southwestern edge of the locality.

neighborhoods.name: Bohnsdorf
neighborhoods.summary: Bohnsdorf is a locality in the borough Treptow-Köpenick of Berlin, Germany. It is located in the south-east of the city.

neighborhoods.name: Rahnsdorf
neighborhoods.summary: Rahnsdorf is a locality of Berlin, Germany, located in the southeast of the Berlin borough of Treptow-Köpenick. Until 2001 it was part of the former borough of Köpenick.

neighborhoods.name: Hermsdorf
neighborhoods.summary: Hermsdorf is a district of Berlin located in the borough of Reinickendorf.

neighborhoods.name: Rosenthal
neighborhoods.summary: Rosenthal is an affluent locality within the Berlin borough of Pankow. The old village first mentioned in a 1356 deed as Rosendalle became a part of Greater Berlin in 1920.

neighborhoods.name: Alt-Tegel
neighborhoods.summary: Alt-Tegel is a Berlin U-Bahn station located on the .t It was constructed by B. Grimmek and opened as "Tegel" station in 1958.

neighborhoods.name: Weißensee
neighborhoods.summary: is a quarter in the borough of in Berlin, Germany, that takes its name from the small lake within it. Before Berlin's 2001 administrative reform, was a borough in its own right, consisting of the quarters of: , , , , and .

neighborhoods.name: Fennpfuhl
neighborhoods.summary: Fennpfuhl is a German locality in the borough of Lichtenberg, Berlin. With a population of 30,932 in an area of , it is the second most densely populated locality in Berlin after Friedenau.

neighborhoods.name: Kaulsdorf
neighborhoods.summary: Kaulsdorf is a locality within the borough Marzahn-Hellersdorf of Berlin. Kaulsdorf was incorporated into Greater Berlin by the Prussian Greater Berlin Act in 1920.

neighborhoods.name: Mahlsdorf
neighborhoods.summary: Mahlsdorf is a locality within the Berlin borough of Marzahn-Hellersdorf. Until 2001 it was part of the former borough of Hellersdorf and has a population of roughly 32000

neighborhoods.name: Nikolassee
neighborhoods.summary: Nikolassee is a locality of Berlin in the borough of Steglitz-Zehlendorf, named after the small Nikolassee lake. Located in the affluent Southwest of the city, the area comprises parts of the Schlachtensee neighbourhood and the eastern shore of the Großer Wannsee lake with the large Strandbad Wannsee lido, as well as the islets of Schwanenwerder and Lindwerder.

neighborhoods.name: Schöneberg
neighborhoods.summary: Schöneberg is a locality of Berlin, Germany. Until Berlin's 2001 administrative reform it was a separate borough including the locality of Friedenau.

neighborhoods.name: Mariendorf
neighborhoods.summary: Mariendorf is a locality in the southern Tempelhof-Schöneberg borough of Berlin.

neighborhoods.name: Rote Insel
neighborhoods.summary: Rote Insel is the name colloquially given to a neighborhood in the Schöneberg district of the German capital, Berlin. As such, the neighborhood is part of Berlin's 7th administrative borough, Tempelhof-Schöneberg.

neighborhoods.name: Mediaspree
neighborhoods.summary: Mediaspree is one of the largest property investment projects in Berlin. It aims to establish telecommunication and media companies along a section of the banks of the river Spree as well as to implement an urban renewal of the surrounding area.

neighborhoods.name: Müggelheim
neighborhoods.summary: Müggelheim is a German locality within the Berlin borough of Treptow-Köpenick. Until 2001 it was part of the former borough of Köpenick.

neighborhoods.name: Hakenfelde
neighborhoods.summary: Hakenfelde is a German locality of Berlin in the borough of Spandau.

neighborhoods.name: Tiefwerder
neighborhoods.summary: Tiefwerder encompasses both a village and a Werder along the Havel River in the Berlin district of Spandau. While the village of Tiefwerder, along with the neighboring southern port of Spandau, falls under the jurisdiction of the district of Spandau, the surrounding forested areas, meadows, and water areas of the Werder are administratively part of the district of Wilhelmstadt.

neighborhoods.name: Tiergarten
neighborhoods.summary: Tiergarten is a locality within the borough of Mitte, in central Berlin. Notable for the great and homonymous urban park, before German reunification, it was a part of West Berlin.

neighborhoods.name: Arkenberge
neighborhoods.summary: The Arkenberge is a hill in the Berlin municipality of Blankenfelde in the borough of Pankow. The name was originally given to a natural hill ridge on the site, and the nearby settlement of Arkenberge was named after that chain of little hills.

neighborhoods.name: Wartenberg
neighborhoods.summary: Wartenberg is a German locality within the borough of Lichtenberg, Berlin. Until 2001 it was part of the former borough of Hohenschönhausen.

neighborhoods.name: Wilmersdorf
neighborhoods.summary: Wilmersdorf is an inner-city locality of Berlin which lies south-west of the central city. Formerly a borough by itself, Wilmersdorf became part of the new borough of Charlottenburg-Wilmersdorf following Berlin's 2001 administrative reform.

neighborhoods.name: Lichtenrade
neighborhoods.summary: Lichtenrade is a German locality within the borough of Tempelhof-Schöneberg, Berlin. Until 2001 it was part of the former borough of Tempelhof.

neighborhoods.name: Marienfelde
neighborhoods.summary: Marienfelde is a locality in southwest Berlin, Germany, part of the Tempelhof-Schöneberg borough. The former village, incorporated according to the Greater Berlin Act of 1920, today is a mixed industrial and residential area.

neighborhoods.name: Alt-Treptow
neighborhoods.summary: Alt-Treptow is a German locality in the borough of Treptow-Köpenick in Berlin. Known also as Treptow it was, until 2001, the main and the eponymous locality of the former Treptow borough.

neighborhoods.name: Plänterwald
neighborhoods.summary: Plänterwald is a German locality within the Berlin borough of Treptow-Köpenick. Until 2001 it was part of the former borough of Treptow and the site of its former town hall.

neighborhoods.name: Rummelsburg
neighborhoods.summary: Rummelsburg is a subdivision or neighborhood of the borough of Lichtenberg of the German capital, Berlin.

neighborhoods.name: Wrangelkiez
neighborhoods.summary: Wrangelkiez, originally known as Schlesisches Viertel, is a Kiez in the Kreuzberg quarter of Berlin, Germany. Wrangelkiez is centrally located within the borough of Friedrichshain-Kreuzberg bordering the Spree river.

neighborhoods.name: Schmöckwitz
neighborhoods.summary: Schmöckwitz is a German locality within the Berlin borough of Treptow-Köpenick. Until 2001 it was part of the former borough of Köpenick.

neighborhoods.name: Heiligensee
neighborhoods.summary: Heiligensee is a locality within Reinickendorf, a borough of the German capital, Berlin.

neighborhoods.name: Borsigwalde
neighborhoods.summary: Borsigwalde is a German locality within the borough of Reinickendorf, Berlin. Until 2012 was a zone part of Wittenau.

neighborhoods.name: Wilhelmsruh
neighborhoods.summary: Wilhelmsruh is a German locality within the borough of Pankow, Berlin. It is the city's smallest locality, after Halensee and Hansaviertel.

neighborhoods.name: Luisenstadt
neighborhoods.summary: Luisenstadt is a former quarter of central Berlin, now divided between the present localities of Mitte and Kreuzberg. It gave its name to the Luisenstadt Canal and the Luisenstädtische Kirche.

neighborhoods.name: Weiße Stadt
neighborhoods.summary: The White City is a large housing estate with 1268 apartments in Berlin's Reinickendorf district. It is one of the six Berlin Modernism Housing Estates and has been listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2008.

neighborhoods.name: Lichtenberg
neighborhoods.summary: Lichtenberg is the eleventh borough of Berlin, Germany. In Berlin's 2001 administrative reform it absorbed the former borough of Hohenschönhausen.

neighborhoods.name: Heinersdorf
neighborhoods.summary: Heinersdorf is a locality in the borough of Pankow in Berlin, Germany. It is located close to the centre of Pankow.

neighborhoods.name: Steinstücken
neighborhoods.summary: Steinstücken, with approximately 300 residents, is a small outlying neighborhood of the Wannsee district in the Berlin borough of Steglitz-Zehlendorf. From the division of Germany in 1949 until a connecting corridor was created in 1971–72, Steinstücken was the only permanently inhabited of twelve original exclaves of West Berlin in East Germany, while West Berlin itself was an enclave controlled by the Western Allies, surrounded by East German territory.

neighborhoods.name: Lichterfelde
neighborhoods.summary: Lichterfelde is a locality in the borough of Steglitz-Zehlendorf in Berlin, Germany. Until 2001 it was part of the former borough of Steglitz, along with Steglitz and Lankwitz.

neighborhoods.name: Gropiusstadt
neighborhoods.summary: Gropiusstadt is a locality within the Berlin borough of Neukölln. It was named after the architect who designed the complex, Walter Gropius.

neighborhoods.name: Johannisthal
neighborhoods.summary: Johannisthal is a German locality within the Berlin borough of Treptow-Köpenick. Until 2001 it was part of the former borough of Treptow.

neighborhoods.name: Wilhelmstadt
neighborhoods.summary: Wilhelmstadt is a German locality of Berlin in the borough of Spandau.

neighborhoods.name: Blankenfelde
neighborhoods.summary: Blankenfelde is a locality located within the Berlin borough of Pankow. Of the city's 95 localities, it is the least densely populated.

neighborhoods.name: Siemensstadt
neighborhoods.summary: Siemensstadt is a locality of Berlin in the district of Spandau.

neighborhoods.name: Hansaviertel
neighborhoods.summary: The Hansaviertel is the smallest Ortsteil of Berlin and is between Großer Tiergarten and the Spree River, within the central Mitte borough of Berlin. The district was almost completely destroyed during World War II but was rebuilt from 1957 to 1961 as a social housing project by international master architects such as Alvar Aalto, Egon Eiermann, Walter Gropius, Oscar Niemeyer, and Sep Ruf.

neighborhoods.name: Fischerinsel
neighborhoods.summary: Fischerinsel is the southern part of the island in the River Spree which was formerly the location of the city of Cölln and is now part of central Berlin. The northern part of the island is known as Museum Island.

neighborhoods.name: Schlachtensee
neighborhoods.summary: Schlachtensee is a locality within the borough of Steglitz-Zehlendorf in Berlin. It was formed as a new administrative district in 2020, combining parts of the Nikolassee and Zehlendorf localities.

neighborhoods.name: Schmargendorf
neighborhoods.summary: Schmargendorf is a south-western locality of Berlin in the district of Charlottenburg-Wilmersdorf. Until 2001 it was part of the former district of Wilmersdorf.

neighborhoods.name: Alt-Tempelhof
neighborhoods.summary: Alt-Tempelhof is a Berlin U-Bahn station on the . It is located under Tempelhofer Damm in the centre of the former village of Tempelhof, now a Berlin district within the borough of Tempelhof-Schöneberg.

neighborhoods.name: Waidmannslust
neighborhoods.summary: Waidmannslust is a German locality within the borough of Reinickendorf, Berlin.

neighborhoods.name: Gesundbrunnen
neighborhoods.summary: Gesundbrunnen is a locality of Berlin in the borough of Mitte. It was created as a separate entity during the 2001 administrative reform, formerly the eastern half of the former Wedding district and locality.

neighborhoods.name: Alt-Mariendorf
neighborhoods.summary: Alt-Mariendorf is a Berlin U-Bahn station located on the line. It serves as the current southern terminus of the line.

neighborhoods.name: Baumschulenweg
neighborhoods.summary: Baumschulenweg is a German locality within the Berlin borough of Treptow-Köpenick. Until 2001 it was part of the former borough of Treptow.

neighborhoods.name: Charlottenburg
neighborhoods.summary: Charlottenburg is a locality of Berlin within the borough of Charlottenburg-Wilmersdorf. Established as a town in 1705 and named after Sophia Charlotte of Hanover, Queen consort of Prussia, it is best known for Charlottenburg Palace – the largest surviving such royal palace in Berlin – and the adjacent museums.

neighborhoods.name: Dorotheenstadt
neighborhoods.summary: is a historic zone or neighbourhood of central Berlin, Germany, which forms part of the locality of Mitte within the borough also called Mitte. It contains several famous Berlin landmarks: the Brandenburg Gate, the Pariser Platz, and Unter den Linden.

neighborhoods.name: Friedrichstadt
neighborhoods.summary: Friedrichstadt was an independent suburb of Berlin, and is now a historical neighbourhood of the city itself. The neighbourhood is named after the Prussian king Frederick I, who founded it in 1691 as the third expansion of the Berlin-Cölln city centre, after Dorotheenstadt and Friedrichswerder.

neighborhoods.name: Nikolaiviertel
neighborhoods.summary: The is an old quarter of the German capital of Berlin, founded . Together with nearby Cölln, they jointly make up Alt-Berlin, the reconstructed historical heart of the city.

neighborhoods.name: Majakowskiring
neighborhoods.summary: The Majakowskiring is an ellipse-shaped street in the Pankow district of Berlin, Germany, in the Niederschönhausen locality. It was famous as the residence of many senior figures in the government of the German Democratic Republic.

neighborhoods.name: Friedrichshain
neighborhoods.summary: Friedrichshain is a quarter of the borough of Friedrichshain-Kreuzberg in Berlin, Germany. From its creation in 1920 until 2001, it was a freestanding city borough.

neighborhoods.name: Oberschöneweide
neighborhoods.summary: Oberschöneweide is a German locality within the Berlin borough of Treptow-Köpenick. It is, with Niederschöneweide, part of the geographic area of Schöneweide.

neighborhoods.name: Friedrichshagen
neighborhoods.summary: Friedrichshagen is a German locality within the Berlin borough of Treptow-Köpenick. Until 2001 it was part of the former borough of Köpenick.

neighborhoods.name: Scheunenviertel
neighborhoods.summary: is a neighborhood of Mitte in the centre of Berlin. It is situated to the north of the medieval Altberlin area, east of the Rosenthaler Straße and Hackescher Markt.

neighborhoods.name: Prenzlauer Berg
neighborhoods.summary: Prenzlauer Berg is a locality of Berlin, forming the southerly and most urban district of the borough of Pankow. From its founding in 1920 until 2001, Prenzlauer Berg was a district of Berlin in its own right.

neighborhoods.name: Stolpe (Wannsee)
neighborhoods.summary: Stolpe is a historic village in the western suburbs of Berlin, the capital city of Germany. It is situated in the locality of Wannsee, in the borough of Steglitz-Zehlendorf.

neighborhoods.name: Onkel Toms Hütte
neighborhoods.summary: is a Berlin U-Bahn station located in the district. Since 12 December 2004 it is served by the line.

neighborhoods.name: Hufeisensiedlung
neighborhoods.summary: The Hufeisensiedlung is a housing estate in Berlin, built in 1925–33. It was designed by architect Bruno Taut, municipal planning head and co-architect Martin Wagner, garden architect Leberecht Migge and Neukölln gardens director Ottokar Wagler.

neighborhoods.name: Großsiedlung Britz (Hufeisensiedlung)
neighborhoods.summary: The Hufeisensiedlung is a housing estate in Berlin, built in 1925–33. It was designed by architect Bruno Taut, municipal planning head and co-architect Martin Wagner, garden architect Leberecht Migge and Neukölln gardens director Ottokar Wagler.

neighborhoods.name: Friedrichswerder
neighborhoods.summary: Friedrichswerder is a neighborhood, situated in the Berliner locality of Mitte, part of the homonymous borough. It is identical to the town of Friedrichswerder, founded in 1662, which was an independent town until 1710.

neighborhoods.name: Lichterfelde West
neighborhoods.summary: Lichterfelde West is part of Lichterfelde in the Steglitz-Zehlendorf borough of Berlin. It is known for its historic mansions, tree-lined streets and green squares.

neighborhoods.name: Niederschöneweide
neighborhoods.summary: Niederschöneweide is a German locality within the Berlin borough of Treptow-Köpenick. It is, with Oberschöneweide, part of the geographic quarter of Schöneweide.

neighborhoods.name: Niederschönhausen
